notes: Car J - the Windows portable desktop shell and full platform guidance (owner item #5). The Electron shell that shipped with car E on Linux now has a real Windows artifact: aidog-desktop-<version>-win.zip, a portable extract-and-run package (no installer, no registry, unsigned by design) built NATIVELY on Windows - WSL drives cmd.exe and the Windows-side Node in an isolated copy so the two platforms never share a node_modules - and verified the only way that counts: the shipped aidog-desktop.exe ran its own --selftest on Windows and answered SELFTEST {ok:true, console:attached, preload:true, ipc:true} against the live console through WSL2 localhost forwarding. The supervisor gained a win32 attach-only gate: when the console is down the shell now fails fast with the honest instruction (start it in WSL2) instead of waiting out a spawn that cannot exist on Windows; macOS keeps its honest not-built label. The zip ships a proper icon generated from the product logo. Platform guidance now covers every system named in the feedback: the install guide gained a Windows section (WSL2 console + native shell + boundaries) and an iOS/Android section (chat channel or SSH-tunnel console, no cloud by design), the site platform rows and README paragraphs tell the same verified truth, and the shell feature doc flips Windows to built-and-verified with the evidence trail (build recipe included: isolated copy, ELECTRON_MIRROR workaround for slow GitHub assets, AIDOG_REPO for standalone runs). Distribution is the GitHub Release asset of this release (CF Pages cannot host a 146 MB zip). Housekeeping: the release-notice pin moved 0.5.72 -> 0.5.73 at kickoff and the source lint now skips build dist directories.
